title: Gentiopicroside inhibits HMGCR/NF-kappaB pathway to alleviate renal fibrosis.
authors: Xu, Qingqing; Zhu, Feng; Song, Ping; Fang, Yuemin; Bai, Zhiqing; Cheng, Tao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究龙胆苦苷通过HMGCR/NF-kappaB通路缓解肾纤维化，核心为小分子-蛋白互作与信号通路，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gentiopicroside (GSP) has been shown to effectively ameliorate renal fibrosis (RF), yet its underlying mechanisms are poorly characterized. This study investigates how GSP alleviates RF using RNA-seq and in vitro experiments. METHOD: First, an RF cell model was established through TGF-beta induced HK-2 cells. The therapeutic effect of GSP on RF was evaluated in vitro through CCK-8 and Transwell assays. RNA-seq was used to identify potential targets of GSP in treating RF, followed by PPI analysis, GO and KEGG enrichment analyses to explore the mechanisms of GSP in alleviating RF. Finally, the mechanisms were comprehensively validated in vitro, and a rescue experiment was conducted by overexpressing HMGCR in HK-2 cells. RESULT: GSP inhibited TGF-beta-induced HK-2 cell proliferation and migration and reduced Collagen I and alpha-SMA expression in vitro. Differential analysis of control vs. model groups revealed a total of 911 differentially expressed genes, including 374 downregulated and 537 upregulated genes. Of these, 225 genes were reversed after GSP treatment. PPI analysis indicated that HMGCR is the core target of GSP in alleviating RF, and molecular docking demonstrated a strong binding between GSP and HMGCR, which was further confirmed by CETSA. GO enrichment analysis revealed that the improvement of RF by GSP is closely related to biological processes such as cholesterol biosynthesis and metabolism. KEGG pathway enrichment analysis highlighted the significant roles of cholesterol metabolism and the NF-kappaB signaling pathway in GSP's effect on RF. Western blot results confirmed that GSP significantly inhibited expression of HMGCR and activation of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway in TGF-beta-induced HK-2 cells. This effect was significantly reversed upon overexpression of HMGCR, indicating that GSP exerts its anti-RF effects by downregulating HMGCR and inhibiting NF-kappaB pathway activation. CONCLUSION: This study confirms that GSP can inhibit the HMGCR/NF-kappaB pathway to protect against TGF-beta-induced HK-2 cell injury, exhibiting favorable therapeutic potential for RF.
abstract_zh: 背景：龙胆苦苷（GSP）已被证明能有效改善肾纤维化（RF），但其潜在机制尚不清楚。本研究利用RNA-seq和体外实验探讨GSP如何缓解RF。方法：首先，通过TGF-β诱导的HK-2细胞建立RF细胞模型。通过CCK-8和Transwell实验在体外评估GSP对RF的治疗效果。使用RNA-seq鉴定GSP治疗RF的潜在靶点，随后进行PPI分析、GO和KEGG富集分析以探索GSP缓解RF的机制。最后，在体外全面验证机制，并通过在HK-2细胞中过表达HMGCR进行拯救实验。结果：GSP在体外抑制TGF-β诱导的HK-2细胞增殖和迁移，并降低Collagen I和α-SMA表达。对照组与模型组的差异分析显示共有911个差异表达基因，包括374个下调基因和537个上调基因。其中，225个基因在GSP处理后逆转。PPI分析表明HMGCR是GSP缓解RF的核心靶点，分子对接显示GSP与HMGCR之间具有强结合力，并通过CETSA进一步确认。GO富集分析揭示GSP改善RF与胆固醇生物合成和代谢等生物过程密切相关。KEGG通路富集分析强调胆固醇代谢和NF-kappaB信号通路在GSP对RF作用中的显著作用。Western blot结果证实，GSP显著抑制TGF-β诱导的HK-2细胞中HMGCR表达和NF-kappaB信号通路激活。过表达HMGCR后，该效应显著逆转，表明GSP通过下调HMGCR并抑制NF-kappaB通路激活发挥其抗RF作用。结论：本研究证实GSP可抑制HMGCR/NF-kappaB通路以保护TGF-β诱导的HK-2细胞损伤，展现出对RF的良好治疗潜力。
